text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Luton Town and Brighton at Kenilworth Road!
In their first fixture following a mid-season break, Luton Town advanced to the fifth round of the FA Cup on Saturday, with a dramatic 2-1 win over Everton.
Now four games unbeaten across all competitions, Rob Edwards' side have a one-point deficit to the 17th-placed Toffees in the Premier League table, having played one game fewer.
However, the Hatters - who could leave the drop zone by winning today - have kept only one clean sheet at Kenilworth Road so far this term.
Like Luton, who they beat 4-1 on the Premier League's opening weekend, Brighton also progressed in the cup last time out, crushing top-flight strugglers Sheffield United 5-2 at Bramall Lane.

Roberto De Zerbi's men remain in the mix for more European football, occupying seventh place in the standings, but their first two league games of 2024 both finished 0-0 - the high-flying Seagulls didn’t have a single goalless draw in 41 matches last year.
Luton make three changes to the side that started last week's win over Everton, as Kaminski, Clark and Osho all return.
While Krul and Townsend drop to the bench, Teden Mengi is not in the squad.
Issa Kabore is still away with Burkina Faso at the Africa Cup of Nations, with Mads Andersen and Jacob Brown among those sidelined by injury.
Steele, Dunk, Milner and Welbeck come in to the Brighton team today, as Verbruggen, Webster, Ferguson and Hinshelwood make way.
Solly March, Joel Veltman, Julio Enciso and Ansu Fati are all injured, while Kaoru Mitoma and Simon Adingra are still on duty at the Asian Cup and AFCON respectively.
The players emerge from the tunnel and out onto the pitch, and kick-off is now just moments away at Kenilworth Road!
Brighton kick off, and we are under way!
LUTON LEAD IN 20 SECONDS!! Adebayo nods in from close range, to give Luton Town an incredibly early advantage.
Ogbene slings over a cross from the right towards Morris at the back post, and the latter's cutback is turned home to put the Hatters 1-0 up! What a start!
Meeting Ogbene's cross, Morris heads the ball back for strike partner Adebayo to score.

LUTON STRIKE AGAIN! Brighton are left floored! The visitors give Lokonga too much time to pick out a pass from midfield, and after Ogbene receives the ball just outside the box, the Irishman beats Steele with his first touch and then strokes the ball into an empty net! It's 2-0 already - incredible stuff at Kenilworth Road, where the home fans are going wild!
Left with space to stride forward and find Ogbene just outside Brighton's box, Lokonga sets up Luton's second goal.
Brighton have now conceded six goals in the first 15 minutes of Premier League matches this season, and no team has shipped more during that time period.

Welbeck slides in to meet a low throughball by Joao Pedro at the back post, but the ex-Arsenal striker can't quite make contact, as Brighton's first serious attack comes to nothing - they've got a long way to come back from here.
Persistent play from Milner - playing his 634th Premier League game today - opens up Luton and ultimately earns his side a corner-kick.
However, following the set-piece, Gross leans back and fires over from outside the box.
Having started so sluggishly, Brighton are slowly regaining their composure now, as they take better care of the ball and build through the thirds.
For the first time, Luton are pushed back.

CLOSE! After escaping down the left flank, Welbeck then drives inside and - with the angle narrowing - drills a low shot just a few inches wide of the right-hand post! Kaminski was diving down at full stretch, but ultimately wasn't required.
For a blatant body-check on Ogbene in midfield, Igor becomes the first player booked by the referee today.
Milner is left lying on the turf, with a pained grimace on his face.
The game comes to a halt as the veteran receives some treatment from Brighton's medics - it looks doubtful that he'll carry on.
As Luton re-start play with a free-kick by Barkley - which just fails to pick out Doughty on the left - Milner stands on the touchline and is surprisingly ready to return.
He'll try to run off his injury and continue.
Following their horror start to today's game, Brighton have conceded 18 first-half goals in 22 Premier League games this season, and only Burnley (19) have leaked more before the break.
It's been decided that Milner can't continue after all, so he limps off to be replaced by young Hinshelwood.
After Barkley rolls a pass across the edge of the Brighton box, Igor closes down Burke's shot from 20 yards and it spins behind for a corner.

SAVE! Again, Barkley is the creator, as he finds Clark inside the area, before the latter unleashes a shot that requires Steele to dive down and tip it away! That could so easily have been three for Luton!
Perhaps fortunate to escape greater punishment, Lokonga follows through in a challenge with Buonanotte, catching the Brighton man with his studs but only being shown a yellow card.
Gross first sees a shot from 20 yards charged down, then Joao Pedro recovers the ball and lays it back to the German midfielder.
However, his second effort harmlessly loops up towards Kaminski.
Luton's resistance remains strong.
Shortly after being booked, Lokonga is over-eager in his attempt to steal the ball from Gross in midfield and topples his opponent.
He's playing a risky game at the moment, and the referee will surely have noted that foul.
Only three of Brighton's last 15 league games have seen the Seagulls succeed, and they are outsiders to take three points from this one now.
Getting at least one goal back before the break would aid their cause, though.
First, Buonanotte misplaces a throughball to end Brighton's attack at one end; then, Luton counter quickly and Adebayo wins a corner-kick on the left.
Doughty's delivery is cleared behind for another corner.
There's nobody in the six-yard box to meet a teasing low cross by Clark from the right, as Luton go forward again.
The Hatters have certainly not sat back since streaking two goals ahead.
A few yards from the left side of the area, Barkley curls a fairly tame free-kick at the target, causing Steele to turn the ball behind for another Luton corner.
Brighton are under pressure here.
Bells upends Buonanotte, conceding a free-kick just over 20 yards from his own goal.
Gross steps up to it, and elects to hang a ball up towards the back post, but after Hinshelwood's nod-down fails to find a team-mate, it is cleared away to safety.
Morris almost slips a cute throughball into Brighton's box, but it's cut out by Hinshelwood.
The latter's raking ball forward for Estupinan, though, is overhit and skips out of play for a Luton throw-in.

ADEBAYO AT THE DOUBLE! More brilliance from Barkley opens up Brighton, and Luton strike again! The ex-Chelsea midfielder steals the ball and then exchanges passes with Adebayo just outside the box, then the latter confidently finds the bottom-right corner to put his side 3-0 ahead! What an incredible first half for the Hatters!
After breaking up play with a smart interception, Barkley plays a nice give-and-go with Adebayo, who then puts Luton three ahead.
Luton have been ruthlessly efficient today, as they've scored three times from four shots on target so far.
It's hard to argue that they're not good value for such a lead, though.
Surely this is their best performance since promotion?
There are to be at least five minutes of additional time at the end of this eventful first half.
Will we be treated to any more goals? Neither side seems too interested in sitting back.
Gilmour lashes over the crossbar with a shot from outside the box, as Brighton's latest attempt to reduce their deficit comes to nothing.
De Zerbi has a big team talk coming up during the break.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 3-0 BRIGHTON
A remarkable first half at Kenilworth Road ends with the home side leading 3-0, having stormed two goals ahead within three minutes.
Luton were out of the blocks before Brighton could blink, as Adebayo headed home from close range, before Ogbene beat Steele to prod into the net just moments later.
While the visitors slightly steadied the ship thereafter, there was more pressure from the Hatters ahead of Adebayo's second strike shortly before the break.
While Brighton now have a mountain to climb, their hosts have an enviable advantage to protect and could be set to escape the relegation zone.
Not only does Brighton's Premier League goal drought go on - the Seagulls last scored a top-flight goal in December - but they are yet to win from behind in the league this season.
Given their arrears today, improving a record of four draws and four losses when trailing at half-time is surely beyond them.
Luton Town kick off, and we are back under way!
Not surprisingly, De Zerbi has responded to his team's predicament by making two half-time changes.
First, Buonanotte is replaced by Ferguson.
Lamptey is also introduced, with Estupinan making way for his fellow full-back.
Being closed down by Lamptey on the edge of Brighton's box, Ogbene tries his luck with a low shot that lacks sufficient pace to trouble Steele.
Still, Luton have come out of the traps in similar style to the first half.
GOAL RULED OUT! Although Clark steers in what appears to be Luton's fourth goal, celebrations are quickly cut short by the assistant's raised flag.
A brief VAR check confirms that he was offside, so it stays 3-0.
Showing some much-needed fight, Joao Pedro gets away from Barkley and then drives a shot at Bell, earning his side a corner-kick on the right.
However, it ultimately comes to nothing.
Lacking options, Steele hangs on to the ball for a while before aimlessly booting the ball long.
Brighton seem lost for ideas, as Luton continue to close down their visitors at every angle - Edwards' game-plan is working perfectly.
Covering his goalkeeper, Dunk dives in to head away a powerful shot by Ogbene, with Steele scrambling across behind him.
That'll be a Luton corner.

ADEBAYO HITS A HAT-TRICK! A corner curled over from the right by Doughty is not cleared by Brighton's static defence, and Adebayo is perfectly placed to head in his third goal of the game from no more than two yards out! Unbelievably, Luton Town now lead the Seagulls 4-0, and their big striker is largely to thank!
Adebayo's eighth league goal of the season confirms him as Luton's top scorer, and it's been quite a game for the Hatters' hitman.
Brighton have simply had no answer to him today.
Brighton are taking better care of the ball now, but they are still making precious little progress.
Luton have them penned inside their own half, with the Kenilworth Road crowd confidently singing about how their club are bound to stay up.
Brighton make a further change, as Baleba replaces Gilmour in midfield.
The action is taking place in a congested midfield now, as Luton aim to suffocate their opponents and see out this game.
They're on course for a famous win here.
Clark deliberately brings down Joao Pedro, who is attempting to escape up the left touchline, and receives a yellow card.
Having sprinted past one opponent and then been brushed by Igor inside the box, Ogbene topples over and claims for a penalty: the referee and the VAR concur that no spot-kick should be awarded.
Nonetheless, the Republic of Ireland winger has been a thorn in Brighton's side today.
Edwards now makes two substitutions: first, Lokonga departs and Mpanzu comes on.
Townsend is also sent on, with the recently booked Clark being withdrawn.
A brief stoppage for Joao Pedro to receive treatment is quickly concluded, and the action resumes.
Luton have just 20 minutes to see out - and with quite a cushion in their favour.
De Zerbi decides to take a cautious approach, with today's game surely a lost cause.
After picking up a knock, Joao Pedro is replaced by Moder.
Hat-trick hero Adebayo departs to warm applause from the Kenilworth Road faithful, as Chong trots on to replace him.
After Osho withdraws from a challenge in midfield, Baleba still dives to the deck.
The referee decides that's simulation, so the Brighton substitute is booked for his troubles.
Ogbene again beats Igor on the right, then his layoff finds Morris, who fires over the crossbar from 15 yards.
The flag goes up for offside in any case, but Luton are not resting on their laurels.

SUPER SAVE! Called into action at last, Kaminski flings himself left to tip away a firm strike at goal by Welbeck! The Brighton striker profited from a lucky bounce to receive the ball just outside the box, then aimed for the bottom-right corner! Lamptey puts the follow-up wide!
Ending a rare spell of Brighton pressure, Lamptey fails to execute a flick over his marker's head following Hinshelwood's throw-in, sending the ball behind for a Luton goal-kick.
That sums up the Seagulls' fortunes today.

STEELE SAVES! Morris is slipped in by Barkley on the left side of the area, but Brighton's goalkeeper is equal to the striker's low shot and repels the ball to safety! Steele stops Brighton conceding a fifth goal, limiting the damage at least a little.
Completing a fine shift in midfield, Barkley walks off, to be replaced by Berry.
Morris, who set up the opening goal within 20 seconds of kick-off, now makes way for Woodrow.
Having won their first two away league games by an aggregate score of 7-2 this season, Brighton have won only one of the next nine.
If today's game ends 4-0, they’ll have conceded 21 goals in the process, netting just nine times in reply.
The story remains similar, as Brighton are having plenty of the ball inside their own half, but Luton's relentless pressure is preventing them from progressing up the pitch.
The Hatters have shown admirable fitness and application.
In a week that saw him linked with some of the most prestigious jobs in European football, this will be a sobering defeat for De Zerbi.
His team have simply not turned up today, while their hosts have been brilliant.
There are to be at least four minutes of stoppage time at the end of this game, which well-beaten Brighton would be glad to finish right now.
Lamptey and Gross combine on the edge of the area, but Osho emerges with the ball and strides forward to set Luton off on a counter-attack.
Almost every player on the home side has contributed to an excellent performance today.
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 4-0 BRIGHTON
A night to remember at Luton Town's inimitable Kenilworth Road headquarters sees the Hatters thump Brighton 4-0, thanks in part to an Adebayo hat-trick.
The striker's first goal came within 20 seconds of kick-off, and Luton led by two soon after, before adding another just before the break.
The Seagulls were left floored when he struck his third just ahead of the hour mark, and they never really recovered, managing only two shots on target throughout.
A masterclass by Edwards caught out the much-feted De Zerbi, and his side now sit outside the Premier League's relegation zone by a point.
Brighton, meanwhile, occupy eighth place, having failed to score in four of their last six matches.
Buoyed by such a stunning result, Luton will visit Newcastle United on Saturday, when Brighton host bitter rivals Crystal Palace.
That's all from today's live coverage, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!
